This topic covers enabling streaming, iterating over the stream using the official SDK, the delta field within each chunk, assembling a full response from deltas, and how streaming applies to both Chat Completions and the Responses API.
1. Enabling Streaming

blocks.alt: Building on the Responses API, streaming responses covers OpenAI specific mechanics

blocks.text: This connects directly to streaming APIs, covered generally in an earlier module, enabling streaming with OpenAI specifically means setting a single parameter, stream, to true on your request, switching the response delivery from a single complete payload to a sequence of incremental chunks.

code.content:
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a short poem."}],
    stream=True,
)

blocks.alt: Setting stream to true switches the response to incremental chunks

blocks.text: 2. Iterating Over the Stream

blocks.alt: The SDK stream object gets iterated in a loop

blocks.text: This connects directly to SDKs, covered in an earlier module, the official OpenAI SDK returns an iterable stream object when stream is set to true, your application code simply loops over it, receiving each incremental chunk as it arrives, without needing to manually parse the underlying server-sent events format.
3. The Delta Field

blocks.alt: A delta field contains the newly generated text piece

blocks.text: Each chunk in the stream carries a delta field, containing just the newly generated piece of text since the previous chunk, rather than the full response accumulated so far, this connects directly to token-by-token delivery covered in the earlier Streaming APIs topic.

blocks.text: 4. Assembling the Full Response

blocks.alt: Each delta gets appended, building the full response over time

blocks.text: Your application appends each incoming delta to a running string as chunks arrive, by the time the stream ends, that accumulated string contains the complete generated response, exactly as if it had been received all at once through a non-streaming call.
5. Streaming With Chat Completions vs the Responses API

blocks.alt: Chat Completions streaming and Responses API streaming both work, with slightly different chunk shapes

blocks.text: This connects directly to the previous topic, both Chat Completions and the Responses API support streaming, with a broadly similar underlying mechanism but slightly different specific chunk shapes, checking the specific documentation for whichever endpoint you are actually using matters for getting the exact field names right.

blocks.title: The underlying concept transfers even when field names differ slightly
blocks.content: Understanding the general concept, incremental chunks accumulated into a full response, transfers directly between these two endpoints, even though the exact field names accessing that content differ slightly between them.

blocks.text: 6. Detecting the End of the Stream

blocks.alt: A signal marks the stream end, letting the iteration loop exit cleanly

blocks.text: The stream naturally ends when the iteration simply stops producing further chunks, the official SDK handles this signal detection internally, your loop simply exits once no further chunks arrive, without needing to manually watch for a specific end marker the way raw server-sent events parsing, covered in an earlier module, would require.
7. Streaming and Tool Use Together

This connects directly to tool selection and execution, both covered in the earlier Agent Prompting module, a streamed response can also involve a tool call, the streaming chunks in that case carry incremental pieces of the tool call arguments rather than plain text content, requiring slightly different handling logic to assemble correctly.

A chat interface enables streaming, iterates over the resulting stream object using the official SDK, appends each delta piece directly to the displayed text as it arrives, producing the progressive, word-by-word display effect covered conceptually in the earlier Streaming APIs topic, now implemented concretely against this specific provider.

Worked Example

A developer initially tries to manually parse the raw server-sent events format from a streaming response, writing custom logic to extract the delta text from each chunk, a genuinely error-prone approach given the specific formatting quirks involved.

Switching to the official SDK simple iteration interface eliminates this manual parsing entirely, the SDK handles the underlying format correctly, letting the developer focus purely on what to do with each incoming delta piece rather than how to extract it in the first place.
Common Mistakes

items: Manually parsing the raw streaming format instead of using the official SDK simple iteration interface
Confusing the delta field, which carries only the newest piece, with the full accumulated response
Not accounting for the slightly different chunk shape when streaming a tool call versus plain text content
Assuming Chat Completions and Responses API streaming use identical field names without checking specific documentation

blocks.text: Practice

Using the official SDK, make a streaming request, iterate over the resulting stream, and print each delta piece as it arrives, then assemble those pieces into the complete final response and compare it against what a non-streaming call to the same prompt returns.
Key Takeaway

OpenAI streaming, enabled with a single stream parameter, returns an iterable stream object through the official SDK, each chunk carrying a delta field with just the newly generated text piece, applying to both Chat Completions and the Responses API, and using the SDK iteration interface avoids the error-prone manual parsing raw streaming formats would otherwise require.
